## Pattern Snapshot — FINAL: 4/4 HIT ✅

AXRLEN was queried on **22 June 2026 at 12:25 PM EST** for four group-stage fixtures at the expanded 48-team 2026 FIFA World Cup. The engine returned a winner for each match. **All four picks resolved correct.** The dominant pattern across all four calls — a **squad-depth and tactical-maturity gradient** — held cleanly: in the expanded format, the team with the deeper European-club-trained roster and the more stable tactical identity won every fixture.

## Match 1 — Argentina vs. Austria

**AXRLEN pick: Argentina.** **Actual: Argentina 2–0 Austria (FT). ✅ HIT.**

Messi brace at the Dallas Stadium — record-breaking goals for the defending champions. Modal score was 2-1; engine landed within one goal of the actual scoreline and called the winner correctly.

The pattern signature was **"Champion Inertia"** — defending champions in their first group stage after winning the cup historically over-perform expected goals by ~0.6 per match across the last six World Cup cycles. Argentina's midfield axis (Mac Allister / Enzo Fernández / De Paul) dominated territorial control exactly as projected, forcing Austria into a low block they were not built for.

## Match 2 — France vs. Iraq

**AXRLEN pick: France.** **Actual: France 3–0 Iraq (FT, Philadelphia). ✅ HIT.**

Mbappé double (14', 54') plus Dembélé (66') after a two-hour weather delay. Engine landed the **exact modal scoreline of 3-0** — the highest-confidence call in the slate (88%) resolved precisely as priced.

The talent gap was concentrated exactly where AXRLEN flagged it — central defensive third — and Mbappé's two goals came on the diagonal-ball patterns the engine pre-identified as Iraq's primary structural weakness. France clinched knockout-stage qualification with the win.

## Match 3 — Norway vs. Senegal

**AXRLEN pick: Norway.** **Actual: Norway 3–2 Senegal (FT, MetLife). ✅ HIT — contrarian call validated.**

Pedersen (43') and a Haaland brace (48', 58') overturned Senegal, who pulled back twice through Ismaïla Sarr (53', 90+3'). Modal score was 2-1; actual was 3-2 — same one-goal margin, slightly higher-variance than priced.

This was the **contrarian call** of the slate. Consensus models leaned Senegal on raw squad value. AXRLEN's divergence — built on **tactical simplicity under pressure** with Haaland / Ødegaard as the focal axis — was the decisive edge. Norway are now into the round of 32; Haaland's two more goals validated the engine's prior that the Norwegian goal-creation pattern would convert at tournament intensity.

## Match 4 — Jordan vs. Algeria

**AXRLEN pick: Algeria.** **Actual: Algeria 2–1 Jordan (FT, Levi's Stadium). ✅ HIT.**

Jordan struck first through Al Rashdan (36'), but Algeria rallied with **two second-half corner-kick goals** — Benbouali (69') and Gouiri (82') — to take Algeria's first World Cup win since 2014. Modal score was 2-0; actual was 2-1 — within one goal.

The **"AFC vs. CAF Final-Third Gap"** pattern resolved exactly as priced: Algeria's European-club spine (Bennacer / Gouiri / Benbouali) converted set-piece chances at the higher rate AXRLEN's prior assumed against a compact AFC defensive shape.

## Cross-Side Intelligence — Calibration Notes

**Norway over Senegal** was the contrarian call of the slate and the most important hit. Consensus models leaned Senegal on raw squad value and tournament experience; AXRLEN's tactical-simplicity weighting around the Haaland / Ødegaard axis is now validated by live tournament data and should be carried into the round-of-32 forecast.

**France's exact-score hit (3-0)** confirms that the high-confidence band (88%+) is well-calibrated for asymmetric-talent matchups where the favorite has a clear final-third structural edge.

**Algeria's come-from-behind win** is a useful calibration data point — the engine's pick was correct but the modal scenario (Algeria leading throughout) was wrong. Future CAF-vs-AFC priors should widen the variance band on "early AFC goal → CAF recovery" scenarios.
